# vendor/ — patched third-party Motoko packages

Packages here are **local forks** of mops registry packages. They exist because a
published version has a bug we cannot wait for upstream to fix, and because
`.mops/` is regenerated by `mops install` — a patch applied there is gone on the
next install, silently.

Each fork is wired in as a local-path dependency, so mops resolves it instead of
the registry copy:

```toml
# mops.toml
icrc1-mo = "./vendor/icrc1-mo"
```

Confirm the override is live with `mops sources | grep icrc1-mo` — it must print
`vendor/icrc1-mo/src`, not `.mops/icrc1-mo@…/src`.

Every local change carries a `LOCAL PATCH` comment. Keep patches minimal and
upstreamable; when upstream releases a fix, drop the fork and go back to a
version string.

## `icrc1-mo` — fork of 0.2.1

**Patch**: `src/ICRC1/lib.mo` → `cleanUpRecents`.

Upstream deletes entries from `state.recent_transactions` (a `mo:core` `Map`)
while iterating it with `Map.entries`. That corrupts the B-tree iterator and
traps with `Natural subtraction underflow` at `core/src/Map.mo:1503`
(`data.count - 1` on a node whose `count` reached 0).

`cleanUpRecents` runs synchronously at the end of every successful transfer
(`handleCleanUp`), so the trap rolls the transfer back. It triggers when a batch
of dedup entries expires in the same pass — i.e. after any quiet period longer
than `transaction_window` (24 h by default) — and it does not self-heal: the
rollback restores the state that traps, so **every** subsequent transfer fails
too.

The fix is the collect-then-delete shape `icrc2-mo` already uses in
`cleanUpApprovals`: gather the expired keys first, delete them after the loop.

Below 32 entries the map is a single leaf and the upstream loop does not trap —
it just silently drops about half the entries it should have deleted, which is
why the leak went unnoticed.

**Regression test**: `pic/dedup_cleanup.test.ts` (build the wasm first with
`bash pic/build-token-wasm.sh`). It is red against upstream 0.2.1 and green
against this fork; `TOKEN_WASM=<path> npx vitest run dedup_cleanup.test.ts`
points it at any build.

**Upstream**: https://github.com/icdevsorg/icrc1.mo — remove this fork once a
release contains the fix.

## `icrc3-mo` — fork of 0.4.3

Copied unpatched from the registry first (its own commit), so each patch below
reads as its own diff. No other dependency imports `icrc3-mo`, so there is one
copy: `mops sources | grep icrc3-mo` must print `vendor/icrc3-mo/src`.

**Upstream**: https://github.com/icdevsorg/icrc3.mo — drop a patch once a
release contains it, and the fork once none is left.

### Patch: an upgraded archive keeps its bounds

**Where**: `src/archive/lib.mo`, the `args` binding.

The archive keeps the arguments it was created with (`maxRecords`,
`firstIndex`, …) in the stable `initial_args`, but reads them through
`transient var args = _args`. A transient variable is re-bound on every
upgrade, and `src/upgradeArchive.mo` upgrades with placeholders
(`maxRecords = 0; firstIndex = 0`). After the ledger's `upgradeArchive`:

- `get_stats` and `remaining_capacity` trap with `Natural subtraction
  underflow` (`args.maxRecords - itemCount`);
- every archive but the first serves the wrong blocks, or traps, because the
  lookup subtracts `args.firstIndex`;
- `append_transactions` reports the archive full (`itemCount >= 0`).

The fix binds `args` to `initial_args`. On a fresh archive the two are the same
value; on an upgrade `initial_args` keeps the creation-time value. The comment
in `upgradeArchive.mo` ("args is stable in archive so these init items are a
noop") states the intent this restores.

**Regression test**: `pic/archive_upgrade_bounds.test.ts`. Red on 0.4.3
(`get_stats` traps right after the upgrade), green on this fork.
`TOKEN_WASM=<path>` points it at any build.

## `mops.lock` caveat (mops CLI 2.13.1)

When mops first resolves a local-path dependency it writes an **absolute** path
into `mops.lock`:

```json
"icrc1-mo": "/Users/<someone>/.../ICRC_fungible/vendor/icrc1-mo",
```

`mops.lock` is committed, so that path has to be made relative by hand — and it
must keep a `./` (or `../`) prefix, otherwise mops reads it as a *version*
(`Package 'icrc1-mo@vendor/icrc1-mo' not found`). The committed form is:

```json
"icrc1-mo": "./vendor/icrc1-mo",
```

Later `mops install` runs preserve it. If a lockfile diff ever shows an absolute
path with someone's home directory in it, put the relative form back.
